newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB SAYS Q4 MARGINS WON'T DISAPPOINT.
newsitem.headline: NAB SAYS Q4 MARGINS WON'T DISAPPOINT.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) managing director Don Argus said on Monday the bank's margins result for the fourth quarter of the year ending September 1997 will not disappoint the market.
"I don't think you'll be disappointed when you see the full year's results," Argus told a Securities Institute of Australia luncheon.
He was referring to a slowdown in the erosion of margins as shown by the third quarter results.
Argus also said the bank remained very acquisitive and observers should not be surprised if NAB formed new alliances to distribute its products.
"We're still an acquisitive bank, very much so," Argus said.
"Don't be surprised if we make announcements on other alliances on how we can push through product in other distribution channels."

"Our Australian financial services group is really through the peak of the lower margins and you can see it in the third quarter results, and I don't think you'll be disappointed when you see the full year's results," he said.
Argus said the addition of value added entities and products was starting to overcome the reliance by old-style bankers on conventional loan products.
NAB continued to try to cut costs, particularly on the technology side, he added. However, he said: "Our costs aren't coming down as quickly as I want them to."
Argus said the creation of a new technology platform at The Yorkshire Bank had not come cheaply. "The paybacks (period) also aren't as short as one might expect," he said.

Argus said NAB also was continuing to try to downsize the corporate centres it had around the world and he said the question had been asked why New Zealand and Australia continued to have separate corporate centres.
"That's not a bad question and that's a question that we're looking at and planning for as we address these cost-related issues," he said.
Argus also said NAB's alliance with electronic cash system operator Mondex was an important initiative.
He also said the bank's involvement in setting up a secure gateway to the Internet was part of a major change in the way banking would be done.
